CardMachine is the model of nova-tools' deleted Lua card machine (02_card_move.lua), kept because CardISA EXTENDS it; it is not the machine lifecycle.go runs. SprintTables is the machine lifecycle.go runs, one action per move of the inventory in docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md section 3 (every place the code writes a primary's column): six states and the lawful moves (Moves, with PR #96's working -> waiting), the named needs as a variable (NeedsSet: needs set and a brief edit's DEPENDS-ON, held to the cycle check), waivers, sentinels and their release, the fleet side (Start, Take, Finish, Withdraw for every working -> ready cause, FleetDown, FleetUp; rework and redo deal a work card), PR #96's NeedsWithdraw and NeedsWait, drop and remove (a removed landed card keeps its outcome), the reads and the accept, and the merge side (each primary's stream, waiting merging stopped or landed with a cause, and its merge cell none queued merged stuck or returned, with Rework, Return, Redo, Merge, MergeGreen, MergeStop, MergeRefused, MergeRed, Resume, Rank and Drop), the outside events and the repair (CiRed, CiGreen, Ack, Crash and Repair: a red CI observation on a placed primary opens the ci judgment, a green observation or an ack closes it, and a crash cuts a step over more than one table before its last write, the work table, leaving the operation pending, the D1 fence, which only repair releases, with the deferred work-table write held for repair). It proves TypeOK, NoNeedCycle, Rule11 (review, merging, landed), AcceptHeld, NeverAcceptBroken, NeverReadByItsWorker, NoCardLostOrTwice, MovesOnlyByTable, ReadyToWaitingOnlyByInsertOrNeeds, WorkingToWaitingOnlyOnNeeds, NeedsWithdrawalWaits, LandedIsFinal, NeedsLandFirst, NeedsHeldIntoWorking, WorkingOnAnUpMember, StreamAfter (G4) and RankRefusesLanded (G6), each rule but TypeOK with a reversed witness (insert, needsany, needless, reviewneeds, dealunmet, cycle, downkeeps, shortaccept, acceptbroken, ownread, skip, landunmerged, returnlost, unland, comeback, withdrawmet, withdrawready, finishunmet, halfstep). A working card, dealt or taken, takes a new need in place and a taken card's finish holds NeedsMet, so no primary reaches review with a need not landed. The refmodel's pending-operation fence (D1: Free) is now held by Crash and Repair (a crash cuts a step before its last write and only repair releases it); refmodel's Accept demands two readers where the code allows one for flash (v1.2.13 cleanups); G3 (ExhaustNote), F3 (a stopped stream's judgment and a skipped repair) and F4/D6 (a cross-stream merge need and a stop on it) are left out. Outside the module: stream moves (MoveCards), admission after the start. Brief replaces one bounded generation, Start captures it per attempt, and Finish bounces an older generation to ready unless explicitly kept; NoOldBriefHeadInReview and the oldheadreviewed witness cover the new rule.

CardISA holds the instruction set of docs/SPEC-ISA.md: one Wait over an operand (resolving a non-wait card alone), a wait card landed by its release (IsaLandEvent, a waiting wait card with released) and never dealt, a result per kind, and LandsOnlyByTable (a card lands from merging, or from waiting a wait card). Four reversed witnesses: doubleland, wrongbase, waitfirst, landanywhere. The upper moves (ready->waiting, working->ready, review/merging reworks) are SprintTables' cards, not this module.

AttemptsEpochs holds the epoch and clear (n, the restore marker, the per-epoch tables, a step's pin, clear as the CAS, a late writer refused as stale, a second concurrent clear, with the noepochcheck witness) and a card's attempt, generation and redeals: Deal cuts a new attempt's work card (attempt + 1, generation 1, refused when it exists already), Redeal deals a withdrawn card again (the same attempt, generation + 1, a redeal counted only when a take of it ended, sprint.FieldTakeEnded), the other generation steps (a stop-return, the live reconcile, a gone lane) step the generation with no redeal, a report naming a generation that is not the live one is refused (StaleGenRefused), and no two launches share an attempt, a generation and an epoch (SuffixUnique, the branch per launch), with the keepgen and nogenguard witnesses. The redeal cap's judgment and the tier ladder are DirtyTick's (RedealsAreEndedTakes, RedealBoundHolds) and SprintRules' (LadderClimbs); the crash cut between AdvanceEpoch and SettleEpoch is a v1.2.14 candidate named in the module and not modelled.

ReadCards holds the read cards (the code asks a card's reads together): MaxReadGen 2 (model bound; readNextGen in code has no cap), the needed count 0, 1 or 2 (ReadsNeededIn), the needed ok read cards count at accept (OkReadsAccept), the merging-short-of-reads return (ShortReadsBack), the live reads (a working read named by its member's beat or returned to the deal within the grace: NoGhostRead, liveness under LiveSpec; internal/sprint/live.go LiveReturns), and four reversed witnesses.

ReadsByRoom now asks a card's reads together (the interim parallel rule of 2026-10-06) with a reversed witness NoAskWhileBroken; the code still counts a re-ask when the reader hands the read back, draws a read from the tier's index, and keeps a begun read on a reader that went away, and zeroes a reader's room under NoRoom or a reader off (readers.go room), none of which the module models (tla/README.md).

Land holds the batch, the check of the caller's epoch before any git, the report fenced to the epoch land read, a refusal of the card's own head reworking it (or reviewing it at its bound) with the stream going on and the lander's own failure stopping it (2026-10-06), and seven reversed witnesses. Land's Repair now skips sentinels, held cards and pushed-unreported cards as check.go Rule6Merging does (Sentinels and HeldCards are nonempty CONSTANTS in the control instance, NoSentinelInQueue and NeverHeldBack are checked, and PushedNeverSentBack extends to Repair with the repairmarked and repairheld witnesses). land.go still does that check. Catalog rows and generated ledgers regenerated inside a batch, the ancestry check named by land-verify-landed-ancestry, repair's atomicity (Rule6Merging reads a snapshot and never re-checks LandingMarked) and the pending fenced operation finish (pending-fenced-op) are not in the module. LandPass holds the pass over several streams (2026-10-07): the merges in parallel up to a width, the landings one at a time in priority order, a pushed tip that passed its own gate, the combined gate, or a clean merge of disjoint files, a landing never lost by the merge after, a collision refusal that stops no stream, a tip recorded as gated only when a gate saw its whole tree (the next pass gates a disjoint merge), a re-merge that merges fewer heads or none, and (2026-10-11) a red gate that blames one head, lands the prefix before it and reworks the head with the stream going on, returns the batch to queued when no head is blamed, and lands the batch whole when the tree tests read none of its files, with NoHeadPastItsBlame and eight reversed witnesses, and the liveness that with every tree green every batch lands; landpass.go runs those two phases. Since 2026-10-10 the landings go as each batch is built (NoHeadOfLine, the inorder witness), each stream's deadline on its own clock from its slot, and LandBisect holds a red batch's blame by bisection (at most ceil(log2 n) gates) and its refusals: a batch is refused only on a bench fault or an environment refusal (a missing tip, a failed diff or reset, a cancelled gate, a remote bench that never ran the gate; RefusedOnlyByBenchOrEnv), with four reversed witnesses. StreamFlowSpec separately models two streams/three batches, protected marks, postmigration card bases (rewrite-all versus preserved working/review cut heads), brief BASE edits, first landing after following sibling trunk advances, certification admission and successful repair. Weakly fair eventual integration and completion have a red/retry counterexample; incomplete terminal states are checked. README records Rowan's cold-read corrections, current Go policy gaps and exact witness mappings. Action mapping: SetBase to streamSetBaseCards/briefOnBase and settings.go sprint.Set writes; BriefEdit to sprint.Brief; StreamLand to landpass runLane/land; CardOntoTrunk to ProtectedLandWhy/placeWhy; StreamMerge/CertDone to the intended global NextStreamMerge (absent at c3b0b1b1) and promoter.step/watch/pending; FollowTrunk and successful Fix are explicit sibling-design/recovery obligations, not implemented guarantees at that head.

For a friend with a live session, hook status and server failure determine up/down; only an explicit coordinator hold yields held while the hook is proven. A one-shot friend (session=one-shot, a member lane) is outside this module: her status is her member's beat by the fleet's PresenceStatus (up, down or held), and no hook record is read for her. Work facts cannot add states. Handover increments generation. Hook protocol internals are modeled by nova-tools Hook.

Holds holds a stream's hold, stop, resume and reopen: holdStream and unhold (a hold withdraws the stream's ready cards, and its working ones with --return), a deal that refuses a held stream while a stopped stream still deals, the cross, red, conflict and rejected stops, a refusal of the card's own head that stops nothing, Resume (a cross stop waits for the needed card to land, a red stop needs --did), TickResume's cross resume, and reopenAdd past a landed stop, with one reversed witness (resumeearly); and the no-stall rule (held.go Unheld): a stop raises an open judgment, NoSilentStall says a stopped stream has an open judgment or is the coordinator's hold, and Progress (a card the coordinator does not hold eventually lands) under fairness of the coordinator's answers, with the reversed witness silentstop; and now a held card, a sentinel and its release (WaitOf in held.go, Resolve, Release and SentinelSet in steps_sentinel.go, SentinelBrief in steps_edit.go, the cut release in sentinel.go): one stream whose line is [a, S, b] (S a plain or a cut sentinel) and one held card h, proving HeldMovesOnlyByRelease, OnlyCoordinatorReleases, CutNeverWaives and SentinelLandsOnlyWhenWaitsUnderWay, with two reversed witnesses (resolveheld, workerreleases). DirtyTick's pump still auto-lands sentinels (stale); a held member stays outside the module.

SprintRules holds twins, the attempt bounds, the failed and bound rules' escalation (the served-tiers skip, the fleet's same failure on three cards left to a mind, a card at its brief's bound left to a mind, a budget exhaustion at its second attempt a tier up), the read-broken rule (below the attempt cap, a finding inside PATHS reworked with it and a file outside PATHS widened in place at most MaxWidens=3 times; every attempt counts toward Cap since the coordinator's last decision, including a widening or deadline, and a coordinator decision opens a fresh window: NoAttemptPastCapWithoutDecision with the reversed witnesses widenresets, ruleatbound and deadlinefree), the harness-fault rework and the late report (a LAND or a HOLD) that finishes a failed attempt, a late report for a stale attempt refused (Part answers, PartsAgree with the reversed witness answersmind), the late rule (a return and redeal once the holder's own deadline is spent, or the one wait is spent) and the late judgment only while its take is live (steps_tick.go TickDeadlines N4 and LateStands: a take withdrawn from outside, no attempt spent, raises none and closes one open: LateOnlyWhileLive), the base gate and the idle alarm, in the same commit as the late-rule code; Part episodes holds a hard pin released past its bound on a running clock that stops while STOPPED, reading the NPinReleased record the tick writes (stops.go PinReleased; PinClockSkipsStopped, with the reversed witness stoppedcounts), the cannot-ask judgment once an unchanged eligible-set episode, and a rule's answer consumed by the attempt it started (2026-10-10). Part judgments holds the three judgment rules (judgment_rules.go ruleFriendTake, ruleReadLate, ruleHoldNeed) with the reversed witness takestarted (FriendKeepsStarted). Part stall holds the landing stall (judgments.go TickLandingStall): the tick end raising one NLandingStall judgment when cards wait in review or merging and the last landing is the bound of running time ago, re-raised each bound, cleared on a landing (StallNotYoung, StallLive), with the reversed witnesses nostall and noclear. Part conflict holds the conflict rule's return of a card whose head the lander refused, reset to flash (rules.go ruleConflict, redo.go landRefused), the same refusal twice a brief defect (ruleBrief), and the redo on the tip (ruleRedo), with one reversed witness (conflictkeeps) and LadderClimbs restated as no rule but the conflict rule lowers a tier. Part noroute holds the no-route rule (seat_answers.go TickRuleNoRoute): a ready card whose tier no route serves, raised past its judgment's deadline to the nearest served tier above and pinned there, never down (NoRouteNeverLowers), only unpinned and ready (NoRouteRaisesOnlyUnpinnedReady) and to the nearest served (NoRouteRaisesToNearestServed), with the reversed witnesses lowers and pinnedraise. Part alert holds the owner alert's send-once (cmd/nova-sprint seat_silent.go tellSeatSilent, seatSilentToken): a raise marked told only after its send (ToldOnlyAfterSend), at most one message a raise across retries and restarts (NoSecondMessage), and every raise told under fairness of the retry (EveryRaiseTold), with the reversed witnesses toldbeforesend and newtoken. Part tier holds the unfunded-tier rule (internal/sprint route.go, steps_tick.go, inbox.go, seat_answers.go): an unfunded tier has exactly one NNoRoute judgment (OneTierJudgment) and quiets per-card and per-stream judgments of its non-working cards (QuietWhileUnfunded) with the reversed witness noquiet (MCSprintRulesTierBrokenNoQuiet); once funded again, the tier judgment closes under fairness of the tick (ResumesWhenFunded). The brief-defect rule (ruleBrief) still has no Part, so the row is partial. Parts reads and answers retain the 2026-10-12 attempt-cap accounting: automatic rework never resets the cap, the bound is answered by a coordinator decision or drop, and findings marked fixed are not read again; reads bounds the number of coordinator decisions by MaxGen, while answers models one such decision before a later bound is dropped. CannotAskClosedWhenEligible requires closure at the next EpTick despite room; OneCannotAskAnEpisode counts only an unchanged eligibility set, with heldeligible and flapeligible reversed witnesses.

Level holds the start-of-tick level as it was before 2026-10-11 (the mean rule and its gap), both end guards, and five reversed witnesses. The code (levelWith, round.levelTo, nextLane) now moves a card only off a member over its width onto a member with a free lane; NeverOffAFreeLane (the free-lane rule, its pass case and a BrokenMeanRule witness) lands with #127, and the row stays partial until it does, while MovesBounded and NeverOnARefuser still describe the code. steps_work.go cites the module. Friend level in internal/sprint/friend_level.go, within a class, and the readers' level are outside the module, which says the readers' level is not modelled. No card named for this map owes friend level, so it is named here rather than as a row with an empty owed_by. The avoid set also holds bench and launch refusals, and the callers are the level op and fleet up's comeUp.

RouteIndex models the counter, the first flag and its preferred draw (FirstPreferred, with the nofirst witness), the per-member harness draw (NeverUnlaunchable per member, with the harnessblind witness), the FieldRoutes exclusion on a new attempt, a resting route skipped as an unserved one (Rested), a read's avoid set (Avoid) and its tier collapse (ReadTier, pro to flash), a redeal, a pinned card, and a read drawn from the reader tier's index beside work cards. Every tier is dealt from its routes, frontier too (LiveSpec, EveryTierIsDealtFromItsRoutes: a work card ready while a member of its pool can launch an entry of its tier leaves ready; MCRouteIndexFrontier, with the frontierfriends witness, the deal that ended an unpinned frontier card before the draw). Still outside the module: a provider at its concurrency budget is not skipped (the deal draws one anyway), and the coordinator's fallback that deals a rework on a full provider.

ServerLanes models the control line (sprint.ControlLine) and the reader-card lease: a batch takes the next ticket and is served first come, first served; the tick takes the line at its turn; a gone caller's ticket is served and handed back; read --begin (a line verb) begins the lease, a served queue renews it (errors ignored), a lease not renewed lapses, and restart keeps the live and takes back the lapsed. Five reversed witnesses (beat on the line, read on the line, a gone write still run, the tick queued like a batch, and norenew); FCFS, TickWaitsOneTurn and LiveLeaseNeverTakenBack hold.
check.go computes violations from a snapshot, so a break is found. Nothing in this tree stores a violation as found, then answered, then cleared, and no module holds that lifecycle.

WorkImport holds an issue under import and a repository's sync, with import and verify each scoped to a subset of the repositories: the import writes only its scope's issues and records the scope in the tree (:scope), verify reads the tree's own scope by default and refuses a --repo outside it, so a verify never reports done outside the import's scope; six reversed witnesses (noreceipt, stale, external, noreopen, partial, scoped). The receipt and Close/Export are design-only. The command guards (an org-wide dry run, an existing output directory, a verify of two trees, later refusals) are outside the module.

DirtyTick deals ahead: Room is DealAhead times the width, a read a whole slot (ReadCost "whole") or half a slot rounded up ("half", read cards); WidthRespected is HoldRespected, and LanesRespected holds the taken cards with the lane acquired at the one writer (the fleet's apply of a take, as takeOne holds the width); the reversed witnesses floorreads and nolanes break the two, MCDirtyTickLanes and MCDirtyTickWidthHalf are their controls. From tla-dirtytick-deal-order-and-skips: DirtyTick holds the tick as shaped on 2026-09-30, plus a member's held and draining status, a run state and the stop, with NeverDealtToDraining, NotAskedOfHeldOrDraining and StoppedMovesNothing; and the deal's held-stream skip (HeldStreamNotDealt; witness dealheldstream) and, under ReadCost "half" (read cards on), its reads-before-work order at a read's half slot (ReadsBeforeWork; witness workfirst; steps_tick.go TickDeal withReadCards, read_cards.go halfLoad); and a refused read-card create never blocks the deal: a refused read is not placed, leaving its card in askwait, and the work deal still runs (OneRefusedReadNeverBlocksWork; witness readblocks leaves the whole pump unapplied; MCDirtyTickReadRefused control, MCDirtyTickBrokenReadBlocks witness). The code deals up to twice a member's width and rebalances the fleet table and the readers table at the start of every tick, and the model has no such step (tla/README.md). Outside the module and cited to their own: friends first (WhoPreference), the bench pool and the staging refusers (RouteIndex Pool), the friend-dealt return (FriendDealtReturn), the fault-hold clear (DealFill FaultHoldClears), and the read card as a dealt entity (ReadCards).

CoordinatorWake holds the batched wake (one wake fires every bus ask the look read, naming three and counting the rest), the filtered message that moves the cursor without a line, and the level events (a judgment, a stop, a friend down) that set and clear between looks; NoLapse is over bus events alone, and LevelSeenWhileItHolds is a level event that holds a whole window waking a run unless it clears first. Three reversed witnesses: nocursor (AtMostOnce), skip and batchdrops (NoLapse), in the same commit as watchwake.go.

NoRoom holds a member's word from Room every tick (draining or not), its beat to the store, and the two planners that read it: the tick's deal and the fleet verbs outside the tick; and the drain the beat says (--draining, Beat.Draining): no deal to a draining member, its dealt cards not taken returned by the level, and a reader row's machine (held or draining) asked nothing, its reads asked and not begun taken back only when another reader can take it (a taker, sweepReads); and the probe gate (known only on a passed probe, steps_work.go fleetStepPlan) that the deal and the ask read (NeverDealtUnknown). Ten reversed witnesses (drainskip, fleetblind, tickblind, drainblind, readblind, silentdrain, noreturn, noreadreturn, probeblind, notaker). The word's staleness (NoRoomNow on a beat's age), a reader's own drain (modelled as its machine's) and the read ask's reader states are outside the module; so is pkg/member never sending --draining (a fork drift for v1.2.13's contraction).

RetireAbsent holds the tick's retirement of a fleet row whose machine record is gone from the inventory: sprint.TickRetireAbsent plans the fleet sync's own removal before the deal (internal/sprint/fleet_retire.go), the store's tick reads the inventory (cmd/nova-sprint/fleetsync.go inventoryMachines -> store.Inventory -> config.Widths, no new store) and deletes the row and the reader reader-<old> DropMembers returned after the answered read (internal/sprint/store/tick.go). RecordsKeepRows is the state invariant (a recorded machine keeps its row) and FleetRowsMatchConfig/LiveRetire the leads-to that the tick closes the gap; a failed read and an answered read that names no record both retire nothing (the code is stricter than the model's failed-read guard). One reversed witness: MCRetireAbsentBroken retires a recorded row on a failed read, the counterexample to RecordsKeepRows.

The requests-per-minute window per model and the concurrency leases per provider, taken by every caller through the server before each model request (WATCH/MULTI, no scripts): NeverOverRate, NeverOverConcurrent and InFlightHeld (each while every renewal inside its bound succeeds; the renewal is best-effort, a renewal not written lets the lease lapse), AbortedWriteReleasesSlot (a lost race releases the slot), Progress, StalledIsGranted (bounded demand), SlotReclaimed; reversed witnesses race (an unguarded write), norenew (the renew-failure case), noexpiry, keepslot (a kept slot after an aborted write). The deal-side fallback and the take gate count fleet cards (Go tests, internal/sprint/rate_budget_test.go), not this module.

RoadmapEntry holds an entry of docs/roadmap.sexp and docs/fixes.sexp under add, remove, pull, note, done and Save's four writes: every group and release keeps an entry, every record names a group or release that is there (a scheduled note's :release is read and not checked), done is final, a shipped release is frozen, a save across the files writes the destination's data first and never loses an entry, and within a file the data is written before its page, with five reversed witnesses (lastchild, sourcefirst, pagefirst, movedone, shippedmove). Note on a done fix or a shipped release is not modelled: the code's Note has no open guard, so its fix card (a v1.2.14 candidate) brings it.

LiveRuns (v1.2.6, 2026-10-10) holds working against the rows' live sets, RUNNING and STOPPED: the tick's reconcile returns a working card its row's fresh live set has not named for the grace since its take or last sighting (WorkingIsLive), a STOP debt entry owns its card only until its return receipt (StopMarkerIsWorking, OwnedLeavesWithReceipt), a held finished report is never returned and does not hold the start back (NoReportLost), a running child's card is never returned (NoRunReturned), a return settles its entry off the debt so clear reads a debt that is owed alone (DebtIsOwed), and no working card of a legacy row (a worker from before v1.2.6, whose beat carries no live set) is returned by the reconcile (LegacyNeverReturned); a take names its card in the live set only at the member's next pass, and the grace from the take covers that lag. Seven reversed witnesses (the v1.2.5 STOPPED tick, a legacy row reconciled as an empty set, the grace dropped, the debt by id, a live set without held reports, a stale beat read as an empty set, a reconcile that leaves its receipt in the debt) and one reachability case. The friend daemon's live set is nova-friend's (nova-tools) and is not in this tree. Since tla-liveruns-settle-by-beat-keeps-a-held-report, SettleByBeat (settleStopDebtByBeat) is in the module: a Legacy row is settled by its stop-returns count alone, so a held report or a child not yet cancelled on a Legacy row is lost or returned (MCLiveRunsSettleByLegacy, NoReportLostAll and NoRunReturnedAll violated): a v1.2.14 candidate, not fixed here, and NoReportLost and NoRunReturned are claimed over the rows whose beat carries a live set.

Adopt holds the seat play as a window: PreCheck's two refusals (no library, a read error) change nothing before the window, then the play's five steps in order (stop, migrate, swap, reinstall, restart), the post-load check and the rescue, with the migration one-way (MigrationIsOneWay) and two reversed witnesses (keep-new fails RefusedLeavesOld, undomigration fails MigrationIsOneWay). The three in-window refusals that exit 1 without reading the old library back (adopt_play.go:236-246, :262-266, :247-249) and the rescue's failed_when: false are v1.2.14 candidates, outside the module.
The digest reads the open set.

A fault is a presence down marked held_by=fault with fault_since, set by the beat-lapse down alone, lifted by faultClear after a beat and an ok finish; a harness fault and a failed take hold by HeldByEnv, and the coordinator's, sync, adopt and env marks stand behind the one person value, all outside. The model's ok reset is stricter than faultCleanFinish's second-resolution stamp compare, which counts a finish in the hold's own second.

An untaken aged card returns with its former friend in its per-card left set, preventing redeal to that friend without banning other work. Running, started and progress work and hard pins are protected. Role, stream, tier and level routing remain outside this bounded model. A one-shot friend is folded in as a member lane (OneShots, MemberTake/MemberFinish: her working card stays working until her member finishes it, OneShotWorkingStays; BadOneShot="bounce" is its reversed witness, MCFriendDealtReturnBrokenBounce), as friendUnstartedWorking, friendDealtReturn and friendLevel skip her seat.

The four friend moves that read cardLeft (friendLevel, friendUnstartedLevel, reclaimUnit, friendCouldTake) are one FriendMove action reading wleft and left; Rework has the brief-defect early return; CapDeal places the card working on her row. Reversed witnesses NoLeft, MachineLeft, CapLeft, RuleLeft and LevelLeft. Rework and CapDeal cite the module; friend_level.go, friend_start.go, friend_deal.go and coordinator_pass.go do not cite it yet, outside PATHS.

The TICKLATE write and the delivery can fail after w.last moved; the model's Restart always recovers it. Since v1.3.6 the seat push loop is retired: the late tick is told the coordinator on the bus by the server's coordinator push (its lateWatch in memory, so a server restart starts the watch afresh, as the "forget" witness), and written as a file by inbox --wait --push <dir>.

The not-held take is its trips (mark, ids, records, keep) outside the lock, the keep behind its revision guard (which prunes work, an efficiency; the serve-time mark check is the correctness guard), the catch-up atomic under the lock, and the entries keyed by <<table, epoch>> with an outside Clear. LoadIsSnapshot holds with the records read as one trip, and LoadIsOfItsEpoch holds that a load takes the records of the epoch it read; the nomark witness drops the serve-time mark check (loadcache.go:154) and fails LoadIsSnapshot, and noepochkey keys entries by table alone and fails LoadIsOfItsEpoch. The card's norevguard witness (the keep's revision guard dropped) is unsatisfiable: dropping the guard explores the same 923,562 distinct states and violates nothing, so it is not added. The records read is one trip, not the code's 1024-record chunks (a v1.2.17 candidate).

ProviderBudget holds the environment-fault hold and the probe gate: probe is the caller's own word (--probe), trusted as the code trusts it, with a reversed witness for every declared witness; the drain (tla-noroom-admission-by-probe) and provider funds (tla-provider-funds) are outside the module.

ReaderTiers holds the ask by tier (freeReaders, ReadsWanted, readerServesTier): a fleet reader's empty tiers cell reads every tier a route serves, a friend's reader (ownModelReader) reads its own model's tiers, an empty cell every tier, four tiers, Need from ReadsNeededIn, and a card's reads asked together; Eligible no longer filters on tier, so NoReadOutsideTier is a real check. Clear keeps member reader rows and working defaults (ShapeOf, SetDefaults). Four reversed witnesses: BugIgnoreHeld fails NoReadToAHeldReader, BugEmptyFlashOnly (a fleet empty cell reads flash alone) fails EmptyCellReadsEveryServedTier, BugClearDropsReaders fails EveryUpMemberIsAReader, and BugClearTurnsOff fails ReadCardsStaysOn.

The ReadyMax bound, per-card holds, the stream, friends, brief, launcher and width causes and timed rests are in; the sentinel's own reason and the balance figure in the reason key (ready_over.go:25-26, a v1.2.14 candidate) are outside.

The coordinator's rest is split timed (coord) and open (coordopen: routes rest with no --until, which ends only by wake), a take in flight across a rest ends refused and is ignored when it was launched before the mark (Launch, Refuse, providerRestsDue e.taken.After(last.Mark())), and the window resets on a provider's rest as well as a route's own; CoordOpenEndsOnlyWoken with the reversed witness MCRouteRestBrokenCoordClock (ExpireProvider ends an open coordinator rest). Since v1.2.17 a provider 5xx under the card's bound (returns < MaxReturns, MaxRateReturns at a small instance) is returned untouched and spends no redeal while it still counts toward the route's window (fivexx; Provider5xxSpendsNoRedeal, Provider5xxReturnsBounded, Provider5xxPastBoundEndsTheTake; reversed witnesses MCRouteRestBroken5xxSpend and MCRouteRestBroken5xxUnbounded); the code numbers each return's record apart (route.go returnTakeNumber), as Counts takes each end. Every MCRouteRest* and MCProviderFunds* case has a current PASS record. Still outside the module: the rate-limit backoff (RateBackoff), the balance arithmetic and payment detection, and the judgments (ProviderFunds).

Sizes: MCDirtyTickReadTwoParts checks the pass case at two keys, another writer's two steps and two parts, with tick parts alone (Kinds {plain}), no display write (MaxD 0), no clear and no queued change (MaxEpoch 0, MaxQ 0), 2.7M distinct states in about 17 s. At the full earlier size it does not fit the 110 s budget on hetzner2: with every kind and the display write it timed out at 110.7 s (over 17.2M distinct states, queue growing); with tick parts alone and the display write it took 106.3 s (23.2M) once and timed out at 110.3 s the next run; with every kind and no display write it took 101.2 s (21.3M), too near the budget to hold. The five earlier witnesses (acquire, halt, catchup, lock, runseq) run at that earlier size with every kind, no clear and no queue; the pass case and the newer witnesses (epoch, startsafterstop, held, nodrain) at one key, one writer's step and one part, with one clear and one queued change.

ServerSwitch holds the server switch and its rollback window: ServerSwitch backs the target up to <target>.prev and copies the candidate over the target, then writes <target>.switch.json when rollback is on (a crash between the copy and the state write leaves the switch without a window); a land pass fault (exit 2) in the window rolls back and removes the state, past the deadline the state is removed and the switch is permanent, and a refusal (exit 1) never rolls back; ServerRollback restores by hand. Four invariants (TargetIsAKnownBinary, RollbackOnlyInWindow, AtMostOneAutoRollbackPerSwitch, NoRollbackOnAHookRefusal), the liveness LandingNeverWaitsOnTheHook, and four reversed witnesses (nodeadline, keepstate, hookfault, hookgate). Since v1.2.16 the machine's landing and the coordinator's are split by identity: the server's own automatic pass (the loop's) is machine work and runs whatever the hook, so an accepted card with the seat unhooked is landed or refused for a reason other than the hook (LandingNeverWaitsOnTheHook, under weak fairness of the pass); a restart drops the hook (SwitchRestart), the seat hooks in again (SeatHooksIn), and only a hand land the gate refuses before it acts (LandHookRefused) is a wait, never a fault, so it never rolls the switch back; the hookgate witness restores the old gate and fails LandingNeverWaitsOnTheHook. It models two facts worth naming: a second switch inside the window overwrites .prev with the first candidate, and a switch with no prior target writes a state whose Previous is missing, so every failure in the window errors. Since v1.2.17 it also holds the lander's standing refusal (landloop.go standRefusal, clearRefusal, judgeRefusal, writeBeat, writeFlight; judgments.go LandRefusalRaise, LandRefusalClose): a refusal is a state, not an event; its first beat raises one judgment (RefusalJudgedAtOnce), the same reason again raises none (AtMostOneJudgmentPerRefusal), every beat it stands names it in place of LAND IDLE (BeatNamesTheRefusal), and every refused landing is eventually reported (RefusalIsReported, the liveness); two more reversed witnesses, silentdedupe (the pre-v1.2.17 dedupe that wrote nothing on a repeated refusal, epoch 20's twenty minutes of IDLE) and latejudge (a judgment only after the stall bound). A refusal stands only when nothing could land (RefusalOnlyWhenNothingCouldLand; LandPartial is a pass of landed and refused batches, never a standing refusal) and is keyed on its normalised reason (sprint.LandRefusalKey); reversed witnesses partialrefusal and rawkey. A cause's text varies pass to pass (Texts) and judgments are counted per cause (raisedFor; witness rejudge); a pass fault before any batch (LandFailed*, "fault") and an unreadable queue (QueueUnreadable, "queue") stand too, judged as "the lander fails every landing" with a LAND FAILED beat line; a round that ran no land clears nothing but a "queue" cause (NoRun; RefusalClearsOnlyWhenItsCauseIsGone, witness idleclears). The judgment is modelled as the store holds it (stored: none, open, acked), a failed write is owed and retried (pending, Recheck), the seat closes it (SeatCloses: ack keeps an acknowledgement, check reopens), a clear closes judgment and acknowledgement; invariant AckSticks, witness ackcloses; a clear's close is owed until it lands (closeOwed, CloseWrite) and nothing is raised before it; a restart (Switch, CrashSwitch, SwitchRestart) loses the loop's memory (known, pending, closeOwed), so the owed close survives only as the store's record, the acknowledgement, and a cause's first raise on a server (LandRefusalRaise) adopts an open judgment but never reads an acknowledgement as said, closing it in the same step as the new judgment (a restart under an acked cause asks once more); invariant StaleSilent (a standing cause held by a stale acknowledgement with no judgment raised in its episode has its raise owed; it replaces NoStaleAck), witnesses staleack and restartack (the owed close lost with a restart, PR 189 read 5); the store coming back is strong fairness on the re-check's write (SF RecheckOk), since a restart disables the re-check between failed writes; the full bounds (two switches, both reasons, the clock to 4) run past the routine runner's 110 s, so MCServerSwitch and MCServerSwitchLiveFull are bench cases (group serverswitch-full, gate bench, the runner's manual mode) and the routine group keeps every witness, MCServerSwitchRoutine (the safety at those bounds with one reason) and MCServerSwitchLive (the liveness at one switch, one reason, the clock to 3); a cause is keyed on its class at the source (code=<class>, landClass), the fold only for a text with none.

Two abstract settings stand for every row of sprint.SettingsWorking; a value changed while RUNNING is outside the gate. The pre-v1.2.17 span reading is not modelled. The card check gate (v1.2.17, start-refuses-until-a-clean-check): check cards writes the epoch's check record (rec clean or failed, recDigest the digest of the cards it checked, recFresh its epoch), a change to the cards (an admit, move, brief, needs, priority or tier edit) moves the digest, a clear leaves the old epoch's record that the store reads as none, and Start is enabled only on a clean record of this epoch whose digest is the cards' now (StartRefusedCheck otherwise); StartOnlyChecked (no start over cards no clean check of this epoch matches) and CleanRecordHasNoDefect, with three reversed witnesses: stalerecord (a change after a clean check starts), failedrecord (a failed record starts) and clearkeeps (a start with no record after a clear). The kinds themselves (sprint.CheckCards) are abstracted to defectOf, fixed per digest: none, warnings only, or a refusing finding (v1.2.18, the warn and refuse split: a same-file finding, or a files finding whose every writer pair the waits order, is a warning); a check fails only on a refusing finding, so WarnsNeverFail (a check fails exactly when the cards hold a refusing finding) and WarnOnlyStarts (a check of warnings alone lets start proceed), with three reversed witnesses: warnrefuses (a warning fails the check), refusewarns (a refusing finding taken as a warning, CleanRecordHasNoDefect) and warngate (start refuses a clean record of cards holding warnings).

ClearDefaults holds the clear's working defaults (sprint.Defaults; docs/SPEC-SPRINT.md section 13, working defaults): settings are epoch keyed, so the advance leaves the new epoch with none, and the clear's set-defaults step (clear.go setDefaults, sprint.SetDefaults) writes each setting still absent, never one a Set of the new epoch wrote: after a clear every plain setting holds its default but one the epoch set (DefaultsAfterClear), every carried setting (the coordinator's threshold alarms, the base) the value of the newest epoch that completed its step, even when a crashed clear is run again (CarrySurvives), a Set of the epoch is never undone (SetSurvives), no setting of a cleared epoch is absent once its step ran (NeverAbsent), and a reader reads each stored value and an absent one by the code's rule, a cleared epoch's default and the first epoch's accessor's own, so no reader of a cleared epoch reads an alarm off for being absent (ReadersSeeWorking, defaults.go clearedDefault). The advance writes a set-defaults owed flag naming the new epoch in the same write (store.EpochState.DefaultsOwed); the owed step is restoreMembers then the defaults, and the flag is cleared only after both (clear.go owedStep, SettleDefaults); a crash anywhere in it is finished by the clear run again, which advances nothing (clear.go finishOwed), only over an epoch the flag names, never an older binary's epoch, a fresh init or epoch 0 (FinishOnlyWhatIsOwed, EpochZeroNeverOwed), and an epoch no longer owed holds its members and readers (MembersRestored). The restore is modelled per row (RestoreRow) and closed by RestoreDone, which writes its marker (the fleet table's members_restored) in the same write as the control cards; two clears run at once (Procs); each restore row write checks, in the same exchange, that the restore is still pending (store.Backend GuardedRows; RestoreSettled when another clear marked it), and no verb edits or removes a row while it is (EditRow, DeleteRow, Start; store.ErrRestorePending), so no clear, the second of two at once included, changes a row, a tier or a control card the epoch wrote (RerunKeepsEpochWrites). Ten reversed witnesses: leaveone, carryadvance, overwrite, nofallback, rerunadvance (a crashed first clear advanced again), markerinfer (the 14caa8b3 inference from a missing marker, an older binary's clear between two of this binary's), restoreskip (the run again without restoreMembers), restorerepeat (a re-run ignoring the marker and writing the tiers unconditionally, as 02af0680 did), noguard (edits and removals landing while the restore is pending), nonatomicrestore (the marker checked once before the restore, as at 90b5ae7d). The start gate over the settings is MachineReady's (StartOnlyWorking).
